purpose: Every legal statement MaraeHub makes, the published page it comes from, and the exact words we rely on. A monthly scheduled task re-reads each monitored page and raises a ClickUp task if the words change or the page cannot be read. It never edits the app. A person decides what a change means.
lastReviewedBy: automated baseline check, not a lawyer

claims.claim: FENZ offers marae a visit to assess fire risks, arranged through its Māori Liaison Officers on 0800 MAHUIKA (0800 6248452).
claims.keyPhrase: see what fire dangers exist in and around your marae
claims.note: Also check the phone number 0800 MAHUIKA (0800 6248452) is still on the page.

claims.claim: A FENZ-approved evacuation scheme may be required for buildings that provide accommodation for six or more people (not counting individual homes).
claims.keyPhrase: accommodation for six or more people

claims.claim: A scheme may be required for buildings used for gatherings of 100 or more people.
claims.keyPhrase: gatherings, for any purpose, for 100 or more people
claims.note: The info sheet words this as 'can hold more than 100 people'. Check both if either changes.

claims.claim: A scheme may be required for buildings that provide employment facilities for 10 or more people.
claims.keyPhrase: employment facilities for 10 or more people

claims.claim: A building owner who does not provide or maintain a required scheme can be prosecuted, and FENZ may seek a court order closing the building (Fire and Emergency NZ Act 2017, ss 76(4) and 79).
claims.keyPhrase: fails to provide or maintain an approved evacuation scheme

claims.claim: A PCBU must provide first aid for workers (Health and Safety at Work (General Risk and Workplace Management) Regulations 2016, reg 13).
claims.keyPhrase: PCBUs have a duty to provide first aid for their workers at work

claims.claim: Adequate first aid equipment, access to it, and enough trained first aiders are required at a workplace.
claims.keyPhrase: must provide adequate first aid equipment for your workplace

claims.claim: Organisations covered by the Act must prepare, maintain and implement an emergency plan (Regulations 2016, reg 14).
claims.keyPhrase: You must have an emergency plan for your workplace

claims.claim: Only certain volunteer organisations fall under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.
claims.keyPhrase: Only certain volunteer organisations fall under

claims.claim: There is no one fire rule for all marae; it depends on building size, sleeping use and age.
claims.keyPhrase: There was no one rule for all marae
claims.note: 2019 news article. Older than the law pages, so treat as background only.
